quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. If it is safe, change lanes and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
It helps catch the attention of other drivers.
You can make eye contact with nearby drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot see. Always turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should you keep distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you time and space to see and react to dangers.
So traffic counters can count you correctly.
So other drivers will cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time and space to see and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: Keeping distance lets you stop or move if the car ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of hazards on the road.

questions.question: What is the purpose of choosing the right lane position?

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: The right lane position helps you see and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle usually needs:

options.text: A complete overhaul before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: More attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more checking than cars. A small problem on a motorcycle is much more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: What makes riding at night safer?

options.text: Other drivers cannot see your turn signals at night.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: When it is clear you are turning, should you use a turn signal?

options.text: Yes, always use a turn signal.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes. Other drivers may not see you, even if you think your move is obvious. There may be vehicles nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, what should you do?

options.text: Check your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small mechanical problem is much more serious on a motorcycle than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Use your turn signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your turn signals, brake light, and lane position properly. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing so other drivers can see you and your motorcycle more easily.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, what should you remember about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are too small to cause problems.
Blind spots require you to turn your head to check.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots require you to turn your head to check.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How do you brake in a straight line with maximum stopping power?

options.text: Apply both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use only the front brake and lock the front wheel.
Use the emergency brake and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: To stop with maximum power in a straight line, apply both brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A person drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago. The body eliminates 1 drink per hour. How many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours since drinking from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks still in the body.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: You don't need to familiarize yourself with it.
Skip the pre-ride inspection if the owner says it's fine.
Spend a few minutes finding all the controls before riding.
Check that the paint is in good condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes finding all the controls before riding.
questions.explanation: Always do the same checks on an unfamiliar motorcycle as you do on your own. Take time to find all controls before you ride because motorcycles differ from each other.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce speed, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges, as they have less grip.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding, what might still happen?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Side effects from drinking may still remain.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects from drinking may still remain.
questions.explanation: Even if you wait one hour per drink, some alcohol can still stay in your body. Your abilities and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riding pants be made from?

options.text: Material that flaps in the wind

questions.correctAnswerText: A heavy material
questions.explanation: Wear pants that cover your whole legs and are made of leather or another tough synthetic material. Clothing should fit snugly without flapping but not so tight it stops your movement.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: When the left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: You should wear riding gloves to:

options.text: Avoid making your hands too hot.
Get a better grip on the handgrips.
Make it easier to use the controls.
Only wear them when it is cool outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a better grip on the handgrips.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of other strong materials when riding. They give you a better grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are slippery and unsafe for motorcycles. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates in the road are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
Watch the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but do not look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead while riding to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react safely before you reach them.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect like:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting your motorcycle to a lower gear slows you down, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What best protects your head and neck during a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to protect your head and neck during a crash.
